multideconv

Source: vignettes/multideconv.Rmd
multideconv.Rmd

This vignette presents a practical, end-to-end workflow for cell type deconvolution with multideconv, including first-generation and second-generation methods, subgroup processing, benchmarking, and downstream machine learning use.

Tutorial

Get started

This tab contains README-level onboarding for installation and basic usage.

For the complete practical workflow, open the Articles tab.

Installation

To avoid GitHub API rate limit issues during installation, configure a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT):

# install.packages(c("usethis", "gitcreds"))
usethis::create_github_token()
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()

Install multideconv from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("VeraPancaldiLab/multideconv")
Basic usage

All outputs are written to a local Results/ folder in your working directory.

setwd("~/path/to/project")
library(multideconv)
raw.counts <- multideconv::raw_counts

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts,
  normalized = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

CIBERSORTx requires valid credentials and Docker configured for non-root use.

Articles

1) Run deconvolution with default signatures

compute.deconvolution() combines multiple methods and signatures on bulk RNA-seq expression data (raw counts or TPM-normalized values with gene symbols).

bulk <- multideconv::raw_counts

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = bulk,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS", "MOMF"),
  normalized = TRUE,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

Use methods, methods_sc, signatures_exclude, and doParallel to customize runtime and scope.

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = bulk,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "DeconRNASeq"),
  signatures_exclude = "BPRNACan",
  normalized = TRUE,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)
deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = bulk,
  methods = "DWLS",
  normalized = TRUE,
  doParallel = TRUE,
  workers = 3,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)
2) Inspect available signatures 
path <- system.file("signatures/", package = "multideconv")
list.files(path)

signature <- read.delim(paste0(path, "CBSX-Melanoma-scRNAseq.txt"))
head(signature)
3) Prepare single-cell inputs and metacells

For large scRNA-seq references, metacells can reduce memory use and execution time before running second-generation methods.

metacells <- create_metacells(
  sc_object,
  labels_column = cell_labels,
  samples_column = sample_labels,
  exclude_cells = NULL,
  min_cells = 50,
  k = 15,
  max_shared = 15,
  n_workers = 4,
  min_meta = 10
)

Example built-in data:

metacell_obj <- multideconv::metacells_data
metacell_metadata <- multideconv::metacells_metadata
head(metacell_obj[1:5, 1:5])
head(metacell_metadata)
4) Run second-generation deconvolution 
deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = bulk,
  normalized = TRUE,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq"),
  sc_deconv = TRUE,
  sc_matrix = metacell_obj,
  sc_metadata = metacell_metadata,
  methods_sc = c("Autogenes", "BayesPrism", "Bisque", "CPM", "MuSic", "SCDC"),
  cell_label = "annotated_ct",
  sample_label = "sample",
  name_sc_signature = "Test",
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

To compute only second-generation methods:

deconv_sc <- compute_sc_deconvolution_methods(
  raw_counts = bulk,
  normalized = TRUE,
  methods_sc = c("Autogenes", "BayesPrism", "Bisque", "CPM", "MuSic", "SCDC"),
  sc_object = metacell_obj,
  sc_metadata = metacell_metadata,
  cell_annotations = "annotated_ct",
  samples_ids = "sample",
  name_object = "Test",
  n_cores = 2,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)
5) Build pseudo-bulk and benchmark signatures 
metacells_seurat <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(metacell_obj, meta.data = metacell_metadata)
pseudobulk <- create_sc_pseudobulk(
  metacells_seurat,
  cells_labels = "annotated_ct",
  sample_labels = "sample",
  normalized = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

Generate signatures from scRNA-seq:

signatures <- create_sc_signatures(
  metacell_obj,
  metacell_metadata,
  cells_labels = "annotated_ct",
  sample_labels = "sample",
  bulk_rna = multideconv::pseudobulk,
  cell_markers = NULL,
  name_signature = "Test",
  methods_sig = c("DWLS", "CIBERSORTx", "MOMF", "BSeqsc")
)

Benchmark against known cell proportions:

benchmark <- compute.benchmark(
  multideconv::deconvolution,
  multideconv::cells_groundtruth,
  cells_extra = c("Mural.cells", "Myeloid.cells"),
  corr_type = "spearman",
  scatter = FALSE,
  plot = TRUE,
  pval = 0.05,
  file_name = "Tutorial",
  width = 10,
  height = 15
)
6) Process cell types and derive subgroup features

compute.deconvolution.analysis() reduces redundancy across deconvolution outputs and builds subgroup-level representations for downstream analysis.

deconv_bulk <- multideconv::deconv_bulk

deconv_subgroups <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconvolution = deconv_bulk,
  corr = 0.7,
  seed = 123,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

Include custom cell names when needed:

deconv_subgroups <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconvolution = multideconv::deconvolution,
  corr = 0.7,
  seed = 123,
  cells_extra = c("Mural.cells", "Myeloid.cells"),
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)
7) Create a deconvolution dictionary

This step links deconvolution-derived features with pathway activity states.

counts <- multideconv::raw_counts
counts.norm <- ADImpute::NormalizeTPM(counts, log = TRUE)
pathways <- CellTFusion::compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm)

deconv <- multideconv::deconv_bulk[rownames(multideconv::deconv_bulk) %in% colnames(counts), ]
deconv_subgroups <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconvolution = deconv,
  corr = 0.7,
  seed = 123,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

deconv_subgroups <- deconvolution_dictionary(deconv_subgroups, pathways)
head(deconv_subgroups[[1]][, 1:5])
print(deconv_subgroups[["States"]])
8) Replicate subgroup definitions in an external cohort 
deconv_1 <- deconv_bulk[1:100, ]
deconv_2 <- deconv_bulk[101:192, ]

subgroups_train <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconvolution = deconv_1,
  corr = 0.7,
  seed = 123,
  return = FALSE,
  file_name = "Tutorial"
)

deconv_subgroups_replicate <- replicate_deconvolution_subgroups(subgroups_train, deconv_2)
9) Use subgroup features in machine learning workflows

To avoid data leakage, build subgroup features inside each training fold and then project to test folds.

library(pipeML)

# traitData_train / traitData_test: clinical labels
# deconv_train / deconv_test: deconvolution matrices
res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  deconv_train,
  traitData_train$Response,
  trait.positive = "R",
  metric = "AUROC",
  stack = FALSE,
  k_folds = 5,
  n_rep = 10,
  feature.selection = FALSE,
  LODO = FALSE,
  ncores = 3,
  return = FALSE,
  fold_construction_fun = prepare_multideconv_folds
)

dt_test <- replicate_deconvolution_subgroups(
  res$Custom_output$Processed_deconvolution,
  deconv_test
)

pred <- pipeML::compute_prediction(
  res,
  dt_test,
  traitData_test$Response,
  trait.positive = "R",
  stack = FALSE,
  maximize = "Accuracy",
  return = TRUE
)
Practical notes
  • If you plan to use CIBERSORTx, provide valid credentials through credentials.mail and credentials.token.
  • Ensure Docker is installed and available for non-root execution if CIBERSORTx is enabled.
  • For patched compatibility with omnideconv, use:
devtools::install_github("omnideconv/MuSiC")
devtools::install_github("omnideconv/SCDC")
  • If you use multideconv in publications, cite multideconv and the underlying deconvolution frameworks and methods used in your analysis.
